solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Whom Mark C replaced and aimed to unmask at the eleventh hour (4,2,4)

indicatorNotes.to unmask: a mask covers the face's edges; taking it off strips AIMED of its outer letters

blocks.note: Mark Carney replaced Justin Trudeau as Canadian PM; written the same way, forename plus initial, he is Justin T
the inside of aIMEd

annotation.surface: A detective story in which someone called Mark C takes over a case and plans to expose the villain at the last moment.
annotation.walkthrough: Mark C looks like a character in a thriller; he is Mark Carney, Canada's Prime Minister, and the clue's own style of forename plus initial tells you to write his predecessor as Justin T.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done at the eleventh hour is done just in time, at the last possible moment.

entries.clue: Dieter’s agreed with working out prank (4)

blocks.note: ja is German for yes, what a German called Dieter says when he agrees
PE = physical education, working out

annotation.surface: Someone on a diet agrees to exercise as a bit of a joke.
annotation.walkthrough: Dieter is not someone on a diet but a German man's name, so his agreement is JA.
annotation.definitionFit: Jape is an old-fashioned word for a practical joke, so it is a plain synonym for prank.

entries.clue: Corporation provides support for music etc from the ground level (7)

indicatorNotes.provides support for: in a down answer, the piece that supports another sits underneath it
indicatorNotes.from the ground: read from the bottom of a down entry upwards, so ARTS goes in backwards

blocks.note: music is one of the arts
a corporation is jokey old slang for a paunch, a tum

annotation.surface: A big company announces it will fund music and the arts at grassroots level.
annotation.walkthrough: Corporation reads as a business sponsor; it is the old joke word for a pot belly, TUM. The words 'ground level' run together in the surface, but 'level' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer or level, of rock or of society.

entries.clue: Futile news I’m surprised to receive when the chips are down (2,2,9)

blocks.note: inane = pointless, futile
'Mercy!' is an exclamation of surprise
gen = information, the news

annotation.surface: Someone is astonished to be told something pointless at a moment of crisis.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is hearing 'I'm surprised' as the exclamation MERCY rather than a statement; GEN is the British slang for information.
annotation.definitionFit: When the chips are down means when things get serious, which is what in an emergency means.

entries.clue: Zealots waving “bye” on board, heading for hell (2,6)

indicatorNotes.waving: the letters of ZEALOTS move about like a waved flag
indicatorNotes.on board: B is put on board, inside the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.heading for: the head, first letter, of Bye

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
the first letter of Bye

annotation.surface: Fanatics on a ship's deck wave goodbye as they sail off to damnation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heading for hell' does double duty: 'heading' takes the first letter of bye, and 'hell' closes the definition, since 'go to blazes' means go to hell.
annotation.definitionFit: To blazes is a euphemism for to hell, as in 'go to blazes'.

entries.clue: London coppers taking against Houses of Parliament painter (5)

indicatorNotes.taking: to take something is to take it in, so MET takes ON into its middle

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
on = against, as in leaning on the wall

annotation.surface: The London police take against a painter at work outside Parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking against' reads as disliking; it splits into the container instruction and ON. Monet painted a famous series of the Houses of Parliament in fog.
annotation.definitionFit: Claude Monet painted the Houses of Parliament many times from across the Thames.

entries.clue: Black suits winning swimmer (4)

blocks.note: spades and clubs are the two black suits in cards
up = ahead, winning

annotation.surface: A card player holding the black suits is ahead of the game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is the crossword's way of saying fish; the scup is a porgy caught off the American Atlantic coast.
annotation.definitionFit: The scup is a fish, and fish are swimmers.

entries.clue: French patriot announced vehicle for exhibition (7)

indicatorNotes.announced: what is announced is spoken, so the letters come from sound

blocks.note: a show van displays goods, and said aloud it matches the French name

annotation.surface: A French patriot is paraded in a display vehicle.
annotation.walkthrough: Nicolas Chauvin was the legendary fanatical soldier of Napoleon who gave us the word chauvinism.
annotation.definitionFit: Chauvin was a (possibly mythical) French soldier famed for his extreme patriotism.

entries.clue: Foremost of foodies with baked topless tarts in mind for son? (6,4)

annotation.type: &lit + charade + substitution + anagram + deletion + first letter
annotation.definition: Foremost of foodies with baked topless tarts in mind for son?

indicatorNotes.baked: the letters of ARTS are cooked into a new order
indicatorNotes.topless: tarts loses its top letter T
indicatorNotes.for: the new letters stand in place of S for son

blocks.note: the psyche is the mind
the S of PSYCHE, which is replaced
tARTS without its T, rearranged, goes in for the S
the first letter of Foodies, which comes last

annotation.surface: A foodie mother bakes tarts with her son in mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: a pastry chef first among foodies, with baked tarts on the mind. 'Topless tarts' is a cheeky surface for tARTS losing its T.
annotation.definitionFit: A pastry chef is a leading foodie whose mind runs on baked tarts.

entries.clue: My parents have run through Italian city (5)

indicatorNotes.have: the parents hold R between them
indicatorNotes.through: R runs through the middle of PA MA

blocks.note: pa and ma, both parents
R = run, as on a cricket scorecard

annotation.surface: Someone's parents have dashed through an Italian city on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run' is R, the cricket abbreviation, split between the two parents.
annotation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in northern Italy, famous for its ham and cheese.

entries.clue: Not many bones broken (2,2,5)

indicatorNotes.broken: the letters of MANY BONES are broken apart and reset

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: An X-ray shows only a few fractures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not many' looks like one phrase, but 'Not' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: By no means is an emphatic 'not', as in 'by no means certain'.

entries.clue: New Romantic style, for sure (4,9)

indicatorNotes.New: the letters are made new, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: The New Romantic look of the 1980s, without a doubt.
annotation.walkthrough: New Romantic reads as the 1980s pop movement, which hides 'New' as the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Most certainly and for sure both express firm agreement.

entries.clue: Pay host, revert to work! (3,6,4)

indicatorNotes.work: the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: Orders at the end of a night out: settle with the host and get back to your job.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the fodder and what you say when the fun is finished.
annotation.definitionFit: Paying the host and heading back to work is exactly what the party's over means.

entries.clue: Facility for genetic engineering support line on which one catches up (1,1,1,7)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, the phrase reads upwards
indicatorNotes.on which: the reversed piece sits on top of the rest in a down entry

blocks.note: I (one) + LAND, catch, as with a fish
a bra is a support garment
RY = railway line

annotation.surface: A laboratory describes a support line that someone grabs onto.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Catches up' looks like a phrase meaning draws level; split it and 'catches' is LAND, 'up' the upward reading.
annotation.definitionFit: A DNA library is a collection of cloned DNA fragments used in genetic engineering.

entries.clue: Tranquillised, deer dizzily came to (8)

indicatorNotes.dizzily: the letters of DEER spin round

blocks.note: numb = deadened, tranquillised
rearranged to ERED

annotation.surface: A deer shot with a tranquilliser dart comes round, still woozy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Came to' reads as regaining consciousness; it is the definition in the sense of amounting to a total.
annotation.definitionFit: A crowd that numbered thousands came to thousands.

entries.clue: One section of cultural significance (6)

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
a conic is a conic section, the curve made by slicing a cone

annotation.surface: One part of something is held to matter culturally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Section' is the geometry sense: a conic section, called a conic for short.
annotation.definitionFit: Something iconic is widely recognised as culturally significant.

entries.clue: Overnight they provided the necessary recommended volume (8)

blocks.note: 'the necessary' is a euphemism for relieving oneself; these pots were kept under the bed for the night
the dictionary British setters and solvers treat as the standard reference

annotation.surface: A hotel supplied everything required overnight, including the suggested reading.
annotation.walkthrough: Chamber pots served the night's needs, and Chambers is also a big British dictionary, the crossword solver's usual reference.
annotation.definitionFit: Chamber pots served the night-time necessities, and Chambers is the dictionary solvers are pointed to.

entries.clue: Releases Come With Me (4,2)

blocks.note: to release is to stop holding on to something
the invitation you give when you want company as you leave

annotation.surface: A music listing: the latest releases include a song called Come With Me.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals dress 'Come With Me' as a song title among new 'releases'; both are simply definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Lets go means releases, and 'Let's go' is an invitation to come along.

entries.clue: If this is set it’s fairly stormy (7)

annotation.definition: If this is set it’s fairly stormy

indicatorNotes.stormy: the letters are thrown about as in a storm

blocks.note: the anagram of IF plus the answer
take IF away from ITSFAIRLY to leave the letters of the answer

annotation.surface: A sailor's rule of thumb: when this sail goes up, the weather is rough.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a compound anagram: IF plus 'this' (the answer) rearranged gives IT'S FAIRLY. As a whole, it describes the sail too, since a trysail is set in heavy weather.
annotation.definitionFit: A trysail is a small strong sail hoisted in storms in place of the mainsail.

entries.clue: Swinger incensing wife visiting northern island (8)

indicatorNotes.visiting: RIB pays a visit inside THULE

blocks.note: Thule, the ancients' far-northern island
rib = wife, from Eve being made from Adam's rib

annotation.surface: A swinger enraging his wife by dropping in on an island in the north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' is not a partner-swapper but something swung, and 'incensing' means giving out incense, not angering. RIB for wife is an old joke from Genesis.
annotation.definitionFit: A thurible is a censer swung on chains to spread incense in church.

entries.clue: The quickest to the buzzer? (7)

blocks.note: reads as the fastest contestant; really the most direct route
reads as a quiz-show buzzer; really an insect that buzzes, whose flight home is famously straight

annotation.surface: A quiz show: who is fastest on the buzzer?
annotation.walkthrough: The buzzer is a bee, and the quickest route to it is the line it flies.
annotation.definitionFit: A beeline is the most direct route, named after the bee, a buzzer.

entries.clue: Unrivalled in the sack, that MC, it’s rumoured (6,7)

indicatorNotes.in: in places one word inside another, so YON sits within BED
indicatorNotes.it’s rumoured: what is rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so sound gives the spelling

blocks.note: the sack is slang for bed
yon = that, in poetry and dialect
a compère is a Master of Ceremonies

annotation.surface: Gossip that a host of ceremonies is peerless between the sheets.
annotation.walkthrough: The racy surface hides three plain pieces; YON is the old word for that, and compère the British name for an MC.
annotation.definitionFit: Unrivalled means nothing can match it, and beyond compare is the idiom for something past all comparison.

entries.clue: What makes bitch bite quarry? (5)

blocks.note: the two letters of bitch that must change to make bite
the change is made by reading one thing as another
the letter of bite that stands where the pair stood

annotation.surface: What provokes a female dog into biting her prey?
annotation.walkthrough: To turn BITCH into BITE you read CH as E, and that instruction spells the answer. The dog surface makes 'quarry' look like part of the question.
annotation.definitionFit: The chase can mean the hunted animal itself, the quarry.

entries.clue: A little bit hard to get into Wilde? (4)

indicatorNotes.to get into: to get into a place is to go inside it, so H goes inside WIT

blocks.note: H = hard, as on pencils
Oscar Wilde was the great wit

annotation.surface: Oscar Wilde's work is a touch difficult to get into.
annotation.walkthrough: Wilde stands for WIT by example, which the question mark signals.
annotation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit'.

entries.clue: Whatever happens, however quickly? (2,3,4)

blocks.note: in any case, no matter what
literally at any speed

annotation.surface: A shrug: whatever happens, and however fast.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is literal: rate as speed, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: At any rate means in any case, and read literally, at whatever speed.

entries.clue: Series included between six and nine nicker (5)

indicatorNotes.included: only the part included in the middle of the number words is kept

blocks.note: tells you to write the numbers out as a run of words
the numbers between six and nine are SEVEN EIGHT; the stretch seveN EIGHt is kept

annotation.surface: A price tag somewhere between six and nine pounds, a nicker being a pound.
annotation.walkthrough: The text to search is not printed: write out the numbers between six and nine, SEVEN EIGHT. Nicker is British slang for a pound, but here it is a horse's soft whinny.
annotation.definitionFit: Nicker is a horse's soft whinnying sound, a gentler cousin of the neigh, so the two are near-synonyms.

entries.clue: Locksmith postpones returning, out of policeman’s custody (4)

indicatorNotes.returning: what is left goes back the other way
indicatorNotes.out of: DS is taken out of DELAYS

blocks.note: delays = postpones
DS = Detective Sergeant, held in custody inside DELAYS; freeing it leaves ELAY

annotation.surface: A locksmith keeps putting off coming back and escapes from police custody.
annotation.walkthrough: The custody is DELAYS holding D and S; free the DS and ELAY reads backwards as the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Linus Yale Jr invented the pin-tumbler lock that bears his name.

entries.clue: The essence of Cavern’s mastery, stirringly staging live Sixties music (6,4)

indicatorNotes.The essence of: the essence is the heart, the middle letter
indicatorNotes.stirringly: the letters are stirred into a new order
indicatorNotes.staging: BE is put on the stage, inside the other letters

blocks.note: the middle letter of CavErn's
anagram fodder with the E
to be = to live, exist

annotation.surface: A review praises the Cavern Club's stirring live show of Sixties music.
annotation.walkthrough: The Cavern was the Liverpool club where the Beatles made their name, so the whole surface belongs to the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Merseybeat was the 1960s Liverpool pop sound of the Beatles and their contemporaries.
